title: code-review-graph — Persistent codebase knowledge graph MCP (49x token reduction)
description: Local knowledge graph MCP server for Claude Code. Builds a persistent structural map of the codebase so Claude reads only relevant files rather than scanning everything. Measured results: 6.8x fewer tokens on code reviews; up to 49x fewer tokens on daily coding tasks (Next.js monorepo: 739K tokens → 15K tokens, 27,700+ files excluded). Installable as a Claude Code plugin via `claude plugin add tirth8205/code-review-graph`. Active development, March 2026. Targets the context-pollution problem for large monorepos specifically.

redundancy_check.notes: No match in registry or completed evaluations. Existing context management (batch-orchestrator, Tool Search Tool, context chunking) all reduce context overhead through different mechanisms. code-review-graph uniquely builds a PERSISTENT structural knowledge graph of the codebase that persists between sessions. The deusdata codebase-memory-mcp (evaluated 2026-03-13) was rejected — check that evaluation to understand how they differ before full evaluation.

evaluation.reasoning: Token efficiency claims (49x) are plausible for large monorepos but need verification. Plugin installation mechanism (`claude plugin add`) is novel and simpler than MCP config. Scored lower on maintenance (50) and community (40) due to no star count mentioned — this is the critical unknown. The deusdata codebase-memory-mcp comparison is key: that tool focuses on AST structural queries (call graphs, dead code); this one focuses on file-relevance filtering (which files to read). Conceptually different use cases. Score would cross 70 if community validation is ≥70 (i.e., 100+ GitHub stars).
research_questions: What is the current GitHub star count for tirth8205/code-review-graph?
Is the plugin mechanism (`claude plugin add`) stable across Claude Code versions?
Are there known stability issues, OOM problems, or session interference (similar to codebase-memory-mcp)?
How does it compare to codebase-memory-mcp architecturally — file-relevance filter vs AST structural queries?
Does the 49x benchmark apply to our actual workspace (~59 projects, mixed sizes) or only to large monorepos (27k+ files)?
evaluation.re_evaluation_trigger: When star count is confirmed ≥100 stars, or when someone tests it on the workspace and reports results.
